input.assignment_instructions:
Start discovery on both targets with minimal HTTP use. Prefer http_request over browser_navigate.

(1) Juice Shop (http://juiceshop:3000). Register each of these as a TargetEndpoint with the suspected CWE and mark it pending_verification:
- GET /ftp/ (use Accept: text/html,application/json). Record whether acquisitions.md is listed, and the .bak files such as package.json.bak.
- GET /encryptionkeys/
- GET /api/Feedbacks (unauthenticated)
- GET /rest/products/search?q= (SQLi candidate)
- POST /rest/user/login (SQLi auth-bypass candidate; JSON body with email and password)
- GET /rest/basket/<id>. Using juiceshop_acct1, find its own basket ID from session_info.own_basket_id and the basket contents. Note acct2's basket ID as well.
- The null-byte path traversal candidate under /ftp/. The raw path /ftp/package.json.bak and the bypass /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md.
Do not exploit anything yourself. Just record each endpoint with the exact method, parameters, session to use, and any basket IDs.

(2) DVWA (http://dvwa), using the dvwa_admin session. Set security=low first. Map these pages and record their form fields, HTTP methods, and the user_token requirement:
- /vulnerabilities/sqli/ (GET id)
- /vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php
- /vulnerabilities/exec/ (POST ip, Submit)
- /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (POST txtName, mtxMessage, btnSign, and the maxlength of each field)
Register separate endpoint entries for low, medium, and high security levels for SQLi and exec. Register xss_s at low only.

Prioritize breadth, so that every candidate is registered as pending_verification.
